summary: Barbara Mittler works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a PhD in Social Anthropology from SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Stella Kramrisch, and Royal W. Weiler. She held professorships at Barnard and Columbia and was president of the AAS in 1990.

Barbra R. Clayton specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University, supervised by Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and studied under G. Raj. She is attested at Mount Allison University in 2013.
Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Amsterdam from circa 1893 to 1906 and later served there as a professor from 1907 to 1944.

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin, later holding posts at KNAW, Heidelberg, Leiden, and the University of Hamburg.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University, holding posts at the Royal Tropical Institute, ANU, University of Munich, University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

Barry Kerzin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and with Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington, CIHTS, and the University of Hong Kong, and founded two medical/values institutes.
Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and has served as an associate professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2026).
Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University. He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1810–1816) and the University of Bonn (circa 1823–1831).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He served as professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hanns Oertel from circa 1932 to 1935. He later served as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who attended Saint Petersburg State University in 1902. He headed the Buryat Scientific Center and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences (1922).

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After completing her PhD at Stanford University in 1987, she held posts at UC Berkeley and Washington University in St. Louis.

Beatrice Erskine Lane was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, and at Columbia University. She was a professor at Otani University beginning in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held academic posts at Maryland, Heidelberg, the University of Hamburg, European University Viadrina, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (circa 1905–1919) and Charles University (circa 1919–1952).
Beiho Takashima was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from circa 1898 to 1901 and later held a post there, also founding the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.

Bela Bhattacharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a post as Professor of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol was a scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
